what_this_is: The D2a-i adjudication record: the MRTR slice of bucket 2a. It is normative for the checks it adjudicates, and Confluence page 275972334 mirrors it. It reuses the record format of MES-126 and the bucket-2 pattern of MES-128 (D2b), and G32 (MCP.Conformance.Adjudications) holds its rows against the bucket-2a view. Its section is OPEN, owned by MES-130, which adjudicates the rest of the view and closes it.
what_this_slice_is: Bucket 2a holds the server-leg OC checks in the declared population that carry no edge in the crosswalk. This slice is the rows whose scenario begins input-required-result-, the MRTR scenarios of SEP-2322. The rest of the view is MES-130's. At the accepted run every row here was SUCCESS except the non-tool pair, which failed; oc_status_at_accepted_run on each row says which.

selector.segments: The tag split on '/', counted from zero: oc:server, then the scenario, the check id and the check name. The selector reads the scenario.
selector.rule: This section's rows are EXACTLY the view rows the selector admits, in both directions. G32 cannot see a selector, so gate 5 holds it: it pins this selector literally and requires the section's keys to equal the selector's result over the view. So the D2a-i and D2a-ii partition is checkable, not hand-listed.
selector.ratified: MES-129 brief (the split view), and PM ratification 29460 (the mechanics stand as planned).

dispositions_added.blocked_on_sdk_gap: The check's behaviour is not implemented by the SDK, or it passes only through a path an SDK gap creates. So no ET-CC unit can honestly be built or extended until a named SDK change lands. The row carries build_level and remedy, meaning the unit to build once the gap is fixed. That unit lands in the same change as the fix, so main never carries a red test (the extend_test precedent). The row also carries sdk_gap: a repository citation of the gap's record (address and bytes) plus the owning ticket.
dispositions_added.sdk_gap: A map: owner (the owning ticket's key), owner_record (one line naming the record that ticket carries: its body's gap heading, or the comment id of each record the row's gap depends on), and record (a repository citation of the gap in this tree). G32 refuses a blocked_on_sdk_gap row without them (sdk_gap_missing), and build_level_missing extends to the new code. Both check shape only. The tightening (PM ratification 29460, Q1): the record cited must be one the owning ticket actually carries, and gaps are cited by address and bytes, never by gap number, because MES-43's body and the sprint 4 escalation table number their gaps independently (MES-43 comment 29459, F2).
dispositions_added.why_green: An optional row field: the mechanism by which a row was SUCCESS when the SDK did not earn it (the fixture, or a gap). Gate 5 requires it on every row that is SUCCESS and blocked_on_sdk_gap; elsewhere it is optional, and this record also carries it on the green generic-validator rows. citation_drift holds its bytes.
dispositions_added.not_added: accept_unmatched is not added: every row here has a remedy.

echo_statement.statement: As on bucket 2b, the bucket-2a view's rows carry only leg and tag, so every row's echo is {} and echo_drift is VACUOUS for this section (CR K4 on MES-126, 29418).
echo_statement.substitute: Each row carries oc_status_at_accepted_run, a repository citation of the check's census entry in docs/conformance/in-scope-2026-07-28.json, from the scenario line of its key through its status line. The name and status lines alone recur here (the generic validator is named once per scenario), so the window runs from the scenario, which makes it unique. G32's citation_drift verifies the bytes. Gate 5 requires the cited scenario and name to equal the tag's segments 1 and 3, the FAILURE rows to be exactly the non-tool pair, both blocked_on_sdk_gap, and every other row SUCCESS.
echo_statement.limit: The substitute guards the adjudication's PREMISE, the status at the accepted run. It does not guard the view: leg and tag are both segments of the key.

emitting_sites.statement: The slice mixes substantive rows and repeated rows. The substantive checks are each emitted by their own scenario's run body. The generic validator WireSchemaValid is emitted by ONE site, run once per scenario, so its rows are one validator repeated, not independent checks. They are reported separately so the repeated rows do not read as independent evidence.
emitting_sites.source: The locator, docs/conformance/oc-emitting-sites-2026-07-28.json: each row's sites. Gate 5 regroups the section's rows by those sites and requires the grouping recorded here.

substantive.note: The scenarios ignore-extra-params and result-type contribute only their generic-validator row: their substantive checks carry an edge and are not in bucket 2a.

null_control_statement.statement: The accepted run has a null-implementation control on this build, docs/conformance/server-2026-07-28-null-control.json. Rows whose check a null server also passes carry null_passability, citing that scenario's entry there. A SUCCESS on such a row is not evidence of SDK behaviour, and none of this record's dispositions rests on one. The gate-5 suite recomputes which rows carry it from the null control, by the rule the row statement gives.
null_control_statement.notable: The non-tool scenario's generic-validator row is passed by the null server and FAILED by the SDK: a server that answers method-not-found sends only valid messages, while the SDK sends an InputRequiredResult body under resultType complete.
null_control_statement.wsv_emitted_assumption: For a generic-validator row the rule assumes the validator was emitted in the null run, which the census cannot show, since it holds counts and names only the failures; the validator emits no check when the implementation sent no message and nothing was violated. It holds on this data. In each such scenario that failed a check, the null run names exactly one failure and counts exactly one SUCCESS, and every other check the locator lists for the scenario is either that failure or emitted only after it passes, so the one SUCCESS is the validator. In each scenario that failed nothing, the null total equals the number of checks the locator lists for it, validator included.

depends_on_fix_statement.criterion: The criterion for depends_on_fix is: the row's remedy, as written, cannot land until D4a's inputRequests object-shape fix lands. That is true when the predicate reads the object shape, when the stimulus is derived from its keys, or when the remedy needs the fixture to emit a keyed map (stateless_handler.ex:30-33, which D4a's row lists as 'Must change with it').
depends_on_fix_statement.statement: Rows meeting the criterion carry depends_on_fix, a pointer to the D4a row that routes that fix as fix_sdk (root cause sdk_typespec_invites_a_list). The pointer is resolved by gate 5, and the fix is counted once, as D4b does for R2. The criterion is applied to every row of the slice, blocked rows included: a blocked row that meets it waits on its sdk_gap AND on that fix.
depends_on_fix_statement.ratified: PM ruling, MES-129 comment 29468 (B1), on CR's finding 29467; it supersedes the set named by 29460, condition (a).

not_carrying.RespectClientCapabilities: The predicate iterates Object.entries(r.inputRequests), which reads a JS array and an object alike, and checks each entry's method; the remedy refutes an elicitation/create entry, which a list admits. No key is read.
not_carrying.InputRequiredResultMissingResponseRerequ: The stimulus is a literal key (wrong_key), not one derived from inputRequests; the predicate tests only the result type.
not_carrying.InputRequiredResultNonToolIncomplete: The predicate tests inputRequests for presence only; the remedy asserts resultType and presence.
not_carrying.NotOnUnsupportedRequests: Neither the stimulus (tools/list, prompts/list, empty params) nor the predicate (resultType) touches inputRequests.
not_carrying.ErrorOnProtocolError: The stimulus is inputResponses null with no key; the predicate tests only error or result type.
not_carrying.ValidateInputResponses: The stimulus is a literal key (user_name) carrying a number; the predicate tests only error or result type.

landing_conditions.rule: The closure rule (PM, MES-129 comment 29472): for every row whose remedy names an unblock or landing condition, the conditions the remedy states EQUAL the records the row cites (sdk_gap.owner_record and depends_on_fix), both ways, and none of them is fixture-earned. Each condition is listed here once, with the phrase that identifies its record in an sdk_gap.owner_record and the token that states it in a remedy. A row's lands_when names its conditions. Gate 5 derives the same set from the row's cited records, THROUGH this catalogue, and requires equality, and requires each condition's token in the remedy exactly when the condition is in lands_when. The catalogue itself is not derived: gate 5 pins it literally, each id with its owner_record_phrase and remedy_token.
landing_conditions.not_held_mechanically: Gate 5 holds tokens against cited records. It cannot hold that the prose around a token says what the token names, nor that a condition is SDK-earned rather than fixture-earned: those are readings, stated per row in the MES-129 correction-round-2 close-out, and are the reviewer's. The catalogue is held by the gate-5 pin, not derived from any record: a new condition fails the pin until the pin is edited, and that edit is the reviewable act.
